scope: Targeted primary-source review for applicability to v18, not an exhaustive bibliography

sources.title: Small Solutions to Polynomial Equations, and Low Exponent RSA Vulnerabilities
sources.applicability: Known-valued modulus and monic univariate degree-d safe form; direct negative neighbor roots exceed N^(1/2). Raw primitive conic fails even the generous XY<=sqrt(W) threshold.

sources.title: Formalizing Coppersmith's Method
sources.applicability: Confirms explicit univariate hypotheses. Existing Isabelle formalization is not a Lean proof of this research problem.

sources.title: Solving Multivariate Coppersmith Problems with Known Moduli
sources.retrieval_status: Official abstract, publisher metadata, and author README read. Direct official PDF retrieval returned 403.
sources.applicability: Optimal shift-space construction and full multivariate recovery are different claims. A solver failure is not a certified empty-root statement.

sources.title: Computing Asymptotic Bounds for the Automated Coppersmith Method via Linear Programming
sources.retrieval_status: Official abstract and author README read; full PDF not obtained. No new numerical bound from this paper is claimed for v18.
sources.applicability: Promising for optimizing a valid bounded polynomial input. Does not by itself supply the missing input modulus and root box in this analysis.

sources.title: Dual Coppersmith: Finding Small Roots Without Multivariate Polynomial Systems
sources.retrieval_status: Author/title and theorems read in mirrored full text. Direct original URL/PDF retrieval failed; do not describe original-host retrieval as successful.
sources.hypotheses_used: Known prime p, bounded modular roots, total-degree shifts, second-successive-minimum separation. Predictive product bound also assumes a Gaussian heuristic and a separate second-minimum model.
sources.applicability: For a box with two exact roots of the raw conic, their independent evaluation vectors violate the sufficient separation condition for any chosen prime modulus. Additional equations or isolated boxes are a separate possible input.

sources.title: Better Bounds for Finding Fixed-Degree Isogenies via Coppersmith's Method
sources.retrieval_status: Official abstract and metadata read in this subtask. Parent separately checked 2026 publication information.
sources.hypotheses_used: Supersingular curves over F_(p^2), specified smooth isogeny degree, four-variable integer small-root construction.
sources.applicability: A finite-field isogeny computation is not an algorithm automatically enumerating all integral points on the current variable curve family.

evidence_boundary: No cited external code was imported or executed. The arithmetic experiment reuses specified v16 elementary routines and is checked by a separately implemented verifier. No new Lean or DeepSeek work.
